outcome: Length of stay in Special Care Nursery (SCN)
cohort: Aboriginal mothers and infants from remote communities in Northern Territory, Australia. Baseline cohort (n=412 mothers, n=416 infants) gave birth between 2004 and 2006. MGP cohort (n=310 mothers, n=315 infants) gave birth between 2009 and 2011.
finding: While not statistically significant, MGP care was associated with more antenatal care, ultrasounds, antenatal hospital admissions, postnatal care, reduced length of stay in SCN, and cost savings, with no difference in major birth outcomes compared to baseline maternity care.
mod_finding: While there was no significant difference in mode of birth between Aboriginal mothers who received Midwifery Group Practice care and those who received baseline maternity care, the MGP group had significantly more antenatal care, ultrasounds, antenatal hospital admissions, and postnatal care in town.
